speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing double vision, weakness in your upper limbs, and difficulty climbing stairs. To understand the severity and location of your issue, can you tell me if your symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and relief with rest is very telling; have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking recently? Also, on a scale of 1 to 10, how much does your double vision interfere with your daily activities?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the fluctuating weakness and specific eye movement issues, I need to check your muscle strength and reflexes immediately. Please lift your arms and legs against resistance while I test your reflexes. REQUEST TEST: Routine_Blood_Work (checking for Creatine Kinase and Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies). REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine.
